title: Initiative Health Sprint: Readout & Investment Lanes
creator: Priya Shah
description: Objective: Produce a concise, decision-ready packet for the mid-cycle strategy sprint that (1) surfaces initiative health across runtime, Dedicated, and Private product lines, (2) proposes reallocation lanes for constrained engineering capacity, and (3) documents explicit KPI asks for exec sign-off. This ticket coordinates PM + Eng + Design inputs, synthesizes telemetry and qualitative signals, and prepares the 12-slide readout for the monthly executive forum. The goal is to have clear yes/no bullets for each investment lane and a fallback plan so the GTM/Platform teams can commit immediately after the readout.
acceptance_criteria: One-page initiative health table with RAG status and 3 leading indicators per initiative (performance, cost, customer adoption)
Three proposed investment lanes with explicit asks (FTE or GPU-hours) and expected delta on target KPIs within 60 days
Executive packet (<=12 slides) uploaded to Confluence with speaker notes and a one-paragraph ask per decision
At least one engineering trade-off analysis per lane (latency vs. cost vs. reliability) linked to the relevant PR/benchmark
Stakeholder sign-off captured in comments from infra-eng, platform-eng, and solutions PMs
comments: 2026-02-21 - Priya Shah: Kickoff meeting notes - scoped 8 initiatives to evaluate (runtime-batching, kv-cache, dedicated-autoscale, private-deploy onboarding, console-rollouts, optimize-quant, evals-regressions, observability-retention). Asked teams to deliver a 1-slide health snapshot by EOD 2026-02-24.

2026-02-25 - Mateo Rivera (Eng): Uploaded latency vs cost bench for runtime-batching. Preliminary finding: continuous batching reduces 95p latency by 12% at 2x throughput, with ~18% token-cost savings when prefix cache hit rate >35%.
2026-02-26 - Nora Patel (Design): Provided readout mockups and a single slide template emphasizing 'Decision, Impact, Ask, Risks' per lane.

2026-02-27 - Discussion (PMs+Eng): Proposed three lanes: (A) Accelerate runtime optimizations (batching + kernel selection), ask: +200 GPU-hours for a 6-week push; (B) Pause low-adoption Private features to free 1 FTE across backend for Dedicated autoscale hooks; (C) Pilot quantized model family on Dedicated for high-throughput customers with a 30-day QA window.
2026-02-28 - Ava Chen: Updated packet to include expected unit-economics delta for each lane and an implementation checklist.
2026-03-01 - Senior PM Review: Requested clearer KPIs tied to customer cohorts (PLG growth vs enterprise contract renewals) and an explicit rollback plan for each lane.
decisions: Provisional exec ask: prioritize Lane A (runtime optimizations) if expected 12-20% unit cost reduction materializes in 6 weeks
If Lane A shows <8% cost reduction at 3-week checkpoint, move 50% of committed GPU-hours to Lane C (quantization pilot)
Pause discretionary Private onboarding work for 4 weeks and reassign one backend engineer to Dedicated autoscale integration
risks: Performance regressions during kernel swaps could increase 95p latency temporarily — mitigation: stage canary on <5% traffic and automatic fallback to current kernels
Customer churn risk for enterprise customers if Private onboarding pauses — mitigation: set communication templates and offer concierge onboarding slots
Overcommitting GPU-hours may delay evals pipeline and regress quality monitoring — mitigation: reserve a 20% buffer for eval runs
timeline: Week 1 (2026-02-20 to 2026-02-26): collect initiative slides, telemetry snapshots, and design mockups
Week 2 (2026-02-27 to 2026-03-05): synthesize packet, run trade-off analyses, finalize asks and KPIs
Week 3 (2026-03-06 to 2026-03-12): exec review, incorporate feedback, public readout and decision capture
next_steps: Lock slides and speaker notes by 2026-03-04
Schedule dry-run with execs and eng leads on 2026-03-06
Post-decision: create targeted Linear tickets (ENG-19283, ENG-19284, PM-37722) with committed scope and owners
